primary.thesis: As of mid-July 2026, NVIDIA is the incumbent largest company. Its lead over the next group (Alphabet, Apple, Microsoft) comes from its AI-accelerator earnings and has been large, on the order of hundreds of billions to about a trillion dollars. Only about 13 trading days remain before July 31, and NVIDIA does not report its own earnings in that window (its fiscal Q2 report comes in late August). The ranking is sticky: closing a gap that size needs a relative move of roughly 15-25% between two mega-caps in two and a half weeks, which is rare without a company-specific shock. Tesla, Saudi Aramco, Amazon and Broadcom are all far below the top tier, so they are simply not contenders. I express the thesis as NVIDIA YES, with NO on the two distant challengers that could only win through an extreme idiosyncratic move.

basket.reason: NVIDIA is the incumbent #1 with a wide cap cushion and no earnings catalyst of its own before July 31, and a leader's position usually persists over short horizons.
Tesla's cap is a fraction of the leaders'. It would need its cap to multiply in weeks, which a Q2 delivery or earnings reaction cannot deliver.
Aramco's value is capped by oil prices and a small free float, and it sits well below the $3T+ tier. Even an oil spike would not lift it to the top.
Broadcom is a large AI-chip name but still well below the trillion-dollar-plus leaders. Its moves also tend to track NVIDIA's rather than overtake it.

failure_narrative: Late July is hyperscaler earnings season: Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta and Amazon report around July 28-30. Suppose one or more of them signals slower AI capex growth, or chooses in-house silicon (TPUs, Trainium, Maia) over NVIDIA GPUs. Alternatively, new US export controls on China, or a Taiwan/TSMC supply scare, could trigger a sharp semiconductor selloff. In either case NVIDIA's multiple compresses by 15-20% or more. Meanwhile Alphabet, rerated on cloud/TPU and Gemini momentum, or Apple/Microsoft as defensive mega-cap havens, hold up or rally after their own earnings. One of them then closes above NVIDIA on July 31 and the C1 leg fails. The NO legs almost certainly still pay, but they cannot offset the loss on C1.
hedge_thesis: In the worlds where NVIDIA loses #1 by month-end, the likely cause is an AI-hardware capex or supply-chain shock rather than a broad market crash, because a broad crash hits every contender roughly equally and leaves the ranking intact. Such a shock would show up in the semiconductor supply chain and in trade policy. Asian foundry and memory stocks (TSMC, SK Hynix, Samsung) would fall, and chip-equipment names (ASML) would weaken. Headlines about Washington tightening export licences, or China retaliating, would multiply. Taiwan-strait risk premia and equity volatility (VIX) would rise. Instruments tied to semiconductor weakness, chip export controls, or Taiwan geopolitical stress would therefore tend to pay in exactly the worlds where the NVIDIA-stays-#1 basket loses.
